hook: A creek, two weathers, and a field sampler.
outcome: Explore concentration, flow and pollutant load, then compare intervention trade-offs.
sources: Curio Class, tools/up-the-watershed/spec.md: synthetic network, loads, flows, areas, costs, intervention reductions and who-pays assignments. Original content CC BY 4.0; code MIT. No observed monitoring data.

EPA, 2012 Recreational Water Quality Criteria, recommendation 1: E. coli 126 geometric mean and 410 STV CFU/100 mL. U.S. government numerical facts, U.S. public domain. https://www.epa.gov/sites/default/files/2015-10/documents/rwqc2012.pdf
EPA, National Primary Drinking Water Regulations: nitrate-N 10 mg/L. U.S. public domain. https://www.epa.gov/ground-water-and-drinking-water/national-primary-drinking-water-regulations
EPA, Quality Criteria for Water (1986): historical lake-inlet phosphorus guideline 0.05 mg/L. U.S. public domain. https://nepis.epa.gov/Exe/ZyPURL.cgi?Dockey=P100P4DO.TXT

EIFAC Technical Paper 1 (1964; journal version 1965): historical numerical sediment bands, independently checked against EPA-600/3-77-042 and British Columbia WQG-18 (2023). Numerical facts only; no FAO prose, figures or dataset bundled. FAO document has no verified permissive licence. https://www.fao.org/4/al950e/al950e00.pdf

EPA agricultural nonpoint-source guidance (2003), urban guidance (2005), Construction General Permit, Municipal Nutrient Removal Technologies Reference Document (2008), BEACH Act program; USDA NRCS standards 382, 390 and 605. U.S. government reference material, U.S. public domain. Intervention types only; efficiencies and prices are synthetic.

Independent fact checks, not imported content: WHO (2018), table B1, E. coli; USGS Circular 1350 FAQ, nitrate; USGS Circular 1136, phosphorus; British Columbia WQG-18 (2023), sediment bands. USGS material U.S. public domain. WHO and BC documents used for verification only.
